scope: Local Windows Codex lifecycle hooks; no benchmark or dataset changes

findings.cause: Original commandWindows uses CMD 'if defined' syntax
findings.evidence: All five original commands reproduced exit code 1 and MissingOpenParenthesisInIfStatement when launched through PowerShell without Paseo environment variables

findings.cause: Original Stop no-op returns empty stdout
findings.evidence: Original CMD Stop command reproduced exit code 0 with empty stdout; the documented Stop contract expects JSON on successful exit

findings.cause: Previous on-disk repair left all five handlers enabled with modified trust definitions
findings.evidence: Read-only hooks/list on the running shared daemon returned enabled=true and trustStatus=modified for all five handlers in all three active project directories

findings.cause: Previous live-daemon diagnostic used the wrong transport
findings.evidence: The control socket is WebSocket over Unix socket; direct JSONL through the byte proxy did not complete initialization. A proper HTTP Upgrade handshake completed initialize and hooks/list immediately

attribution_limit: No persisted hook failure events were found in inspected logs, history tables, or recent rollout tails. Original defects are reproducible; individual historical UI failure entries cannot be conclusively mapped to them from the available records.

repair.operation: Set enabled=false only for the five user Paseo hook state entries through config/batchWrite with expectedVersion and reloadUserConfig=true
repair.reason: All inspected running Codex processes lack Paseo session markers; these optional notifications are unused in the current windows

usage.future_paseo_use: If Paseo notifications are needed again, review the corrected command definitions and re-enable the handlers through Codex /hooks
